html:
The Sakurabiat, also called Mekens, are a small people of the Rio Mequéns area in Rondônia, western Brazil. Their language belongs to the Tupari branch of the Tupian family, close to that of the Tupari and Makurap.

In the first half of the 1900s rubber tappers moved into the region during and after the rubber boom. Disease and forced labour cut their numbers to a few dozen. They now hold a small Indigenous territory, and fewer than a hundred people speak the language.
